label: Week 37, 2026
recap:
The week was quiet, with seven bill movements, four case updates, and one federal document. Activity spanned four jurisdictions: California led with four items, while New Jersey, New York, and the United States Congress each had one. One item was unthemed.

Children and minors was the largest theme at three, covering companion chatbots, age verification, school use, and protections for people under eighteen. Transparency and disclosure followed at two, on labeling AI output and impact assessments. Consumer protection and discrimination, health care, and workforce and education each appeared once. One agency, the Health and Human Services Department, was noted.

federal.title: Medical Devices; Cardiovascular Devices; Classification of the Cardiovascular Machine Learning-Based Notification Software
federal.detail: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the cardiovascular machine learning-based notification software into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the cardiovascular machine learning- based notification software. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.

reading.body:
No bills moved, no cases advanced, and no federal documents were recorded in US AI policy between September 7 and 13, 2026.

The week produced no measurable activity across any tracked category: legislation, litigation, or federal agency action. This absence could reflect genuine lull, gaps in data collection, or the summer-fall transition typical in policy cycles. Without positive indicators of movement, the record shows only silence.

The lack of activity means nothing can be inferred about regulatory momentum, court precedent, or agency priorities during this period. This data documents what did not happen rather than what did.
